metadata.name: Banque Saudi Fransi (BSF)
metadata.provenance: financials built 27-Nov-26 from BSF FY24/FY25 Annual Reports & 9M26 Tadawul Statements; quotes await [BBG]

observations.notes: FY24 assets SAR 292.78bn, net loans SAR 204.17bn, deposits SAR 185.12bn, net profit SAR 4,544m.
FY25 assets SAR 309.01bn (+5.5%), net loans SAR 214.89bn, deposits SAR 195.22bn (+5.5%), net profit SAR 5,353m (+17.8%), impairments -16% YoY.

9M26 assets SAR 338.6bn (+10% YTD), loans SAR 230.4bn (+7% YTD), deposits SAR 203.2bn, NSCI SAR 6,863.1m (+6.0% YoY), net profit SAR 4,376.6m (+6.9% YoY), CET1 15.3%, Tier-1 18.1%, CAR 20.2%, NPL 0.95% (165.3% coverage).

verdict.stance: Neutral / Well-Capitalized Saudi Corporate Bank (15.3% CET1, 0.95% NPL)
verdict.summary: BSF is a core Kingdom corporate bank (SAR 338.6bn assets in 9M26) anchored by Kingdom Holding (~16.2%) and strong internal capital (15.3% CET1, 20.2% CAR). Asset quality tightened further to 0.95% NPL with 165.3% coverage while 9M26 net profit rose 6.9% YoY.

positives: Strong capital stack: 15.3% CET1, 18.1% Tier-1, 20.2% Total CAR in 9M26.
Pristine asset quality: 0.95% NPL ratio with 165.3% provisioning coverage.
Solid 9M26 earnings trajectory (+6.9% YoY net profit to SAR 4.38bn; +6.0% NII).
negatives: Elevated loan-to-deposit ratio (~113% in 9M26: loans SAR 230.4bn vs deposits SAR 203.2bn) requires ongoing wholesale/DCM funding.
Rate-cut sensitivity on floating-rate corporate loan yields.

background.business_overview: Leading Saudi corporate, treasury, and retail bank (formerly Credit Agricole affiliate).
background.asset_perimeter: SAR 230.4bn net loans & advances (9M26) heavily weighted to prime Saudi corporates.

recent_drivers: 9M26: Assets SAR 338.6bn (+10% YTD), net profit SAR 4,376.6m (+6.9% YoY), CET1 15.3%, CAR 20.2%, NPL 0.95% (165.3% coverage).

catalysts.impact: Confirms full-year ROE, LDR normalization, and 2027 NIM guidance.

catalysts.event: Q1 2027 Senior EMTN / Capital Issuance Window

management_guidance_tracker.variance_analysis: Tier 2 & AT1 issues plus earnings boosted CAR >20%.

management_questions.question: Outline funding roadmap to bring LDR down from ~113% without compressing NIM.
Assess corporate credit demand across Vision 2030 contractors vs non-oil private sector.
Confirm call economics on 6.375% AT1 and appetite for senior sukuk/EMTN supply in 2027.
